_comment: Vernacular material map — which construction materials a region's geology/ecology makes local, for the style-derivation step (docs Part 10, the brief->build pipeline). The PRINCIPLE (build with what's at hand) is the grounding; the region->material pairings are the canonical vernacular set. 'engine_materials' maps each to a material in resources/materials.json; WANTED = not yet in the atlas (docs/WantedAssetsBacklog.md). Wall thicknesses live in structure_styles.json.
principle: Pre-industrial vernacular building uses locally-available materials: stone where it outcrops, timber where forests stand, clay where it is dug, reed/straw for thatch. Transport was costly, so geology + ecology dictate the walls + roof. (Brunskill, Illustrated Handbook of Vernacular Architecture.)

stone_upland.description: Hard-rock uplands (moor, fell, dale) — stone is the default.
stone_upland.source: stone vernacular in stone country (Brunskill); dry-stone walling 1.4-1.6 m (The Stone Trust, cited)

lowland_timber.description: Wooded lowland clay vales — timber frame + earth infill, thatch or tile.
lowland_timber.source: timber-frame + wattle & daub lowland vernacular (Brunskill); exterior wall ~0.222 m (buildingconservation.com, cited in structure_styles timber_cottage)

chalk_cob.description: Chalk / cob country (downland, the south-west) — cob or chalk-block walls, thatch.
chalk_cob.source: cob ~0.6 m walls in chalk/clay regions (Devon/Dorset vernacular); flint where it occurs. Cob/flint/chalk thickness to_ground.

brick_clay.description: Brick-earth regions (East Anglia, the Low Countries) — fired brick once kilns + fuel exist.
brick_clay.source: brick vernacular where brick-earth + fuel (later-medieval onward; GENRE-FLAG earlier periods)

fen_reed.description: Fen / marsh / reed-bed — reed thatch, timber, little stone.
fen_reed.source: reed thatch (Norfolk reed) in fen country; the longest-lived thatch

_to_ground: Per-region wall thicknesses live in structure_styles.json (cob/flint/chalk-block thicknesses are to_ground). The region->geology assignment for a given world is a world-gen/biome input (biomes.json), not yet wired into the style derivation.
